title: Check: spreading and priority
description: Five questions on even placement and what happens when the cluster is full.

questions.prompt: What does `maxSkew` control in a topology spread constraint?

options.text: The largest permitted difference in Pod count between topology domains

questions.explanation: maxSkew: 1 across zones means no zone may hold more than one Pod above the least-populated one.

options.text: The Pod schedules anywhere if the constraint cannot be met
The Pod stays Pending if the constraint cannot be met

questions.explanation: The alternative is ScheduleAnyway, which downgrades the constraint to a scoring preference.

questions.prompt: What does a higher-priority PriorityClass do when the cluster is full?

options.text: It can preempt lower-priority Pods, evicting them to make room
It raises the Pod's CPU limit
It moves the Pod to another cluster

questions.explanation: Preemption evicts lower-priority Pods so the higher-priority one fits. `preemptionPolicy: Never` opts out.

questions.prompt: What does `globalDefault: true` on a PriorityClass mean?

options.text: Pods with no priorityClassName get this priority

questions.explanation: Only one PriorityClass in the cluster may set it.

questions.prompt: Which object stops a voluntary disruption from taking too many replicas down at once?
questions.explanation: A PDB is what makes `kubectl drain` wait instead of evicting everything. It does not constrain involuntary disruptions like a node crashing.
